body.text: Plugging temperature indicators (PTIs) are one way to monitor sodium purity.
body.cite: Word: Plugging Temperature Indicators.docx, slide 1.5 Sodium Purity Monitoring Theory

checks.q: Which of these is NOT a reason given for keeping sodium coolant pure in a sodium fast reactor?
o: To minimize the risk of material activation by neutron irradiation
To reduce the cost of reactor operation
To prevent corrosion of structural materials
To enhance heat transfer efficiency
checks.x: The lesson plan's reasons are preventing corrosion, enhancing heat transfer and minimizing material activation. Reducing the cost of reactor operation is the wrong choice on its question.

body.text: As sodium gets colder and approaches its freezing point:
body.cite: Word: Plugging Temperature Indicators.docx, slide 1.7 Plugging Temperature Indicator

body.text: A PTI uses this to measure the level of impurities in the sodium. Sodium is sent through the PTI and gradually cooled.
body.cite: Word: Plugging Temperature Indicators.docx, slide 1.5 Sodium Purity Monitoring Theory

body.text: When the sodium at the orifice reaches the impurity saturation temperature, impurities such as oxygen and hydrogen begin to precipitate and deposit on the orifice surface, which changes the sodium flow rate. The temperature measured when the flow begins to decrease is the plugging temperature.
body.cite: Word: Plugging Temperature Indicators.docx, slide 1.7 Plugging Temperature Indicator

checks.q: At what moment is the plugging temperature measured in a plugging temperature indicator?
o: When the flow past the orifice begins to decrease
When the sodium first enters the indicator
When the flow stops completely
When the sodium reaches its boiling point
checks.x: The temperature measured at the moment the flow begins to decrease is the plugging temperature.

body.text: So the lesson plan's text names two parts: the orifice, where the impurities deposit, and the flow meter, which detects the flow decrease. The diagrams of the rest of the indicator are pictures in the lesson plan and are not used.
body.cite: Word: Plugging Temperature Indicators.docx, slide 1.5 Sodium Purity Monitoring Theory

checks.q: Which device detects the flow decrease in a plugging temperature indicator?
o: A pressure relief valve
A cesium trap
An ion chamber
A flow meter
checks.x: When a flow meter detects the flow rate decrease, the temperature of the sodium is noted.

body.text: A cold trap cools a small fraction of the main flow to just above the sodium freezing point, so impurities precipitate and adhere to the mesh packing and walls. The clean sodium returns to the main loop.
body.cite: Word: Plugging Temperature Indicators.docx, slide 1.8 Cold Trap

checks.q: How can plugging temperature indicators support cold trap operation?
o: They remove cesium ahead of the trap
They show cold trap effectiveness and when a trap should be placed in service
They provide the cooling flow to the trap
They regenerate a saturated trap
checks.x: PTIs can be used to determine the effectiveness of cold traps, and when they should be placed in service if not operated continuously.

checks.q: Why does the Natrium Sodium Processing System operate with the sodium above the saturation temperature?
o: To keep the sodium from boiling
To increase cesium removal
To reduce pump power
To avoid plugging passageways in the system
checks.x: The SPS operates with the sodium above this saturation temperature to avoid plugging passageways in the system.

body.text: A PTI has one limit. It:
body.cite: Word: Plugging Temperature Indicators.docx, slide 1.11 Advantages of PTI Fill-in-blank

body.text: It does detect the impurity's presence, and it offers these principal advantages over grab sampling:
body.cite: Word: Plugging Temperature Indicators.docx, slide 1.11 Advantages of PTI Fill-in-blank

body.text: PTI analysis is not delayed by radioactive decay periods before a sample can be removed, which were up to five days on the EBR-II primary sodium system.
body.cite: Word: Plugging Temperature Indicators.docx, slide 1.11 Advantages of PTI Fill-in-blank
Word: Plugging Temperature Indicators.docx, slide 1.11 Advantages of PTI Fill-in-blank

body.text: PTIs give a continuous measurement, or one that can be repeated at short intervals. This helps identify the cause of unexpected changes in impurity concentrations after operations such as reactor shutdown, cold trap isolation or fuel handling.
body.cite: Word: Plugging Temperature Indicators.docx, slide 1.11 Advantages of PTI Fill-in-blank

checks.q: Why are on-line plugging temperature indicators free from the error of impurity segregation seen in grab samples?
o: The sample is held for five days first
The indicator identifies each impurity species
No sample cools in a container, where impurities can segregate to the walls
The sample is diluted with argon first
checks.x: On-line systems are not subject to analytical errors caused by segregation of impurities to the walls of a container during cooling of sodium samples.

body.cite: Word: Plugging Temperature Indicators.docx, slide 1.11 Advantages of PTI Fill-in-blank

body.text: From 1964 to 1967 they were the principal indicators of sodium purity. The practice was to run without cold trapping until the plugging temperature exceeded 149°C, then run the cold trap until it fell below 107°C, then shut the trap off again.
body.cite: Word: Plugging Temperature Indicators.docx, slide 1.11 Advantages of PTI Fill-in-blank

body.text: More-or-less continuous cold trap operation began in 1967, with plugging temperature measurements made once per day.
body.cite: Word: Plugging Temperature Indicators.docx, slide 1.11 Advantages of PTI Fill-in-blank

body.text: Copper in the primary sodium was discovered in 1967 by the irreversible plugging of the PTI.
body.cite: Word: Plugging Temperature Indicators.docx, slide 1.11 Advantages of PTI Fill-in-blank

Heat exchanger tubing
Fuel cladding
The cold trap mesh
checks.x: The source of the copper was found to be the exposed bus bars of the primary auxiliary pump.

examples.title: Reading a PTI during the EBR-II years
examples.page: Word: Plugging Temperature Indicators.docx, slide 1.11 Advantages of PTI Fill-in-blank
examples.problem: It is 1965 at EBR-II, the cold trap is off, and the indicated plugging temperature has just exceeded 149°C. Using the practice of those years, what happens next?
steps: A plugging temperature above 149°C meant it was time to operate the cold trap.
The cold trap ran until the indicated plugging temperature was below 107°C.
The cold trap was then shut off again.
examples.answer: Run the cold trap until the plugging temperature is below 107°C, then shut it off.
examples.cite: Word: Plugging Temperature Indicators.docx, slide 1.11 Advantages of PTI Fill-in-blank

facts.q: What part of a plugging temperature indicator do impurities deposit on?
facts.a: An orifice. The deposit reduces the flow, which a flow meter detects.

facts.q: What can plugging temperature indicators tell you about a cold trap?
facts.a: How effective it is, and when it should be placed in service if it is not operated continuously.

facts.q: How did EBR-II discover copper in its primary sodium?
facts.a: By the irreversible plugging of the PTI in 1967. The source was the exposed bus bars of the primary auxiliary pump.

facts.q: Since when have PTIs been used at EBR-II?
facts.a: Since the initial fill of sodium in the primary and secondary systems in 1963.

facts.q: What is the key process indicator for sodium purity at Natrium?
facts.a: The saturation temperature, which correlates directly with impurity concentration.

facts.q: How do on-line PTIs avoid sample contamination?
facts.a: On-line systems avoid contamination of the sample by air or other foreign agents.
